records.entity: United States Mint deep-storage vault, Fort Knox, KY
records.name_as_stated: Mint Held Gold - Deep Storage / Gold Bullion / Fort Knox, KY
records.relation: holds its gold reserves in custody
records.summary: The largest single block of United States gold, 147,341,858.382 fine troy ounces, sits in deep storage in the US Mint's depository at Fort Knox, Kentucky, on the Treasury's own facility-by-facility report.
records.detail: The US is a split case: the gold itself belongs to the Treasury, not to the Federal Reserve, which holds gold certificates against it. The Treasury's Status Report of U.S. Government Gold Reserve, published as a monthly dataset by the Bureau of the Fiscal Service, lists holdings by facility. The row for 31 October 2026 gives facility 'Mint Held Gold - Deep Storage', form 'Gold Bullion', location 'Fort Knox, KY', 147,341,858.382 fine troy ounces, book value USD 6,221,097,412.78. The record date 2026-10-31 is the record_date field in that row.
records.source_note: Raw JSON from the Treasury's own API for the dataset 'Status Report of U.S. Government Gold Reserve' (human-facing page: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/status-report-government-gold-reserve/u-s-treasury-owned-gold). Values read from the raw response, not from a fetch summary.

records.entity: Federal Reserve Bank of New York vault
records.name_as_stated: Federal Reserve Bank Held Gold / Federal Reserve Banks - NY Vault
records.relation: holds its gold reserves in custody
records.summary: The portion of the United States gold stock that is not in Mint deep storage sits in the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's vault: 13,376,987.724 fine troy ounces of bullion plus 73,452.066 ounces of gold coins.
records.detail: The Treasury's Status Report of U.S. Government Gold Reserve for 31 October 2026 splits its rows into 'Mint Held Gold' and 'Federal Reserve Bank Held Gold'. Under the latter, location 'Federal Reserve Banks - NY Vault' carries 13,376,987.724 fine troy ounces of gold bullion (book value USD 564,805,851.07) and 73,452.066 ounces of gold coins (USD 3,101,307.82). Two further Fed rows, location 'Federal Reserve Banks - Display', hold 1,993.321 ounces of bullion and 377.434 ounces of coins across unspecified Reserve Banks. The metal remains Treasury property; the report is the depositor's own accounting of where it is kept. TWO CURATORIAL NOTES. First, the entity is named as the VAULT rather than as the institution because merge_links.py refuses a domestic gold-custody record whose entity name contains no place word, on the ground that the popup would otherwise read as a bank holding its gold in custody of itself. That guard is right for this case: the Federal Reserve Bank of New York is part of the same central banking system as the depositor, so only the vault is the place. A second node will therefore exist alongside the institution node 'Federal Reserve Bank of New York', which is the custodian nine other countries use. THAT IS DELIBERATE AND SHOULD NOT BE FOLDED: one node is the NY Fed acting as custodian for foreign central banks, the other is the vault where United States gold sits. Expect dup_parties.py to flag the pair as a subset match and leave it. Second, the United States is a genuinely odd case on this row and the owner may want to render it differently: the metal is owned by the Treasury, not by the Federal Reserve, which holds gold certificates against it. So the depositor here is the state rather than the central bank, which is not true of any other record on this row.
records.source_note: Raw JSON from the Treasury's own API for 'Status Report of U.S. Government Gold Reserve'; human-facing page https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/status-report-government-gold-reserve/u-s-treasury-owned-gold. Entity spelling matched to the existing map party 'Federal Reserve Bank of New York' in party_names.json.

records.summary: The National Bank of Kazakhstan's audited 2025 consolidated accounts split its gold by where it sits, and the largest line, 14,239,574,101 thousand tenge, is gold bars in the National Bank's own vault.
records.detail: National Bank of the Republic of Kazakhstan, Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, Note 14 'ЗОЛОТО' (Gold), pages 97-98. The note's table has three blocks: 'Золото в слитках в хранилище НБК' (gold bars in the NBK's vault) 14,239,574,101 thousand tenge at 31 December 2025 against 5,208,748,898 a year earlier; gold on deposit with foreign banks, 1,025,128,196; and gold in the accounts and vaults of foreign banks, 8,858,285,834; total 24,122,988,131. The note names no city for the NBK vault and names none of the foreign banks, grading them only by credit rating. Figures read from the raw pdftotext extraction of the PDF, not from a fetch summary.

blanks.read: KAZ converted on the domestic half but is a documented blank on the foreign half. National Bank of the Republic of Kazakhstan, Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, Note 14 'ЗОЛОТО' (pp. 97-98, read in full): 1,025,128,196 thousand tenge of gold sits on deposit with foreign banks and 8,858,285,834 thousand tenge in the accounts and vaults of foreign banks, but the note identifies those banks only by credit-rating band (AA-, A- to A+, BBB+, AAA). The continuation page adds that at 31 December 2025 the gold on the accounts of two counterparties each exceeded 10% of the NBK's equity, and still does not name them. The only institution named anywhere in the note is the London Bullion Market Association, and that is the price fixing used for valuation, not a custodian. The note also names no city for the NBK's own vault. Route for a later round: the NBK's separate (non-consolidated) statements, or its gold and foreign-exchange asset management reports.

Bank Negara Malaysia Annual Report 2024, 'Our Finances' chapter (ar2024_en_ch4.pdf, 4,145,875 bytes, downloaded and extracted in full, 30,858 characters). Note 3 'Gold and Foreign Financial Assets' gives Gold RM14,556 million (2023: RM11,884 million) as one line beside Securities, Deposits and bank balances, and Others, and states nothing about where the gold is. Accounting policy note 2.5 'Gold' says only that gold is stated at fair value with unrealised gains and losses taken to the Risk Reserve. The words custody, custodian, safekeeping, vault, London, Bank of England and Settlements do not occur anywhere in the financial statements chapter. BNM publishes no location for its gold in this document.

Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago Annual Report 2025 (cbtt-annual-report-2025-revised-08.05.26-may-2026.pdf, 13,078,758 bytes, downloaded and extracted in full, 291,595 characters). Accounting policy note 's. Gold holdings' covers only valuation: gold at year-end market price, a single gold valuation in Trinidad and Tobago dollars per troy ounce, gains or losses on gold 'held by the Bank' recognised only when realised. Gold then appears only as a line in the fair-value hierarchy table and in the revaluation-reserve movement table, and in the statistical appendix column 'Gold Reserves'. Every occurrence of the word gold in the document was read; none gives a location, an institution or a country. The words custodian and vault occur in the document but never in connection with gold (custodian pricing of investments; a currency-processing machine in the Bank's vault).

Wrong document, and worth recording so the next round does not repeat it. 'Laporan Kelembagaan Bank Indonesia 2025' (bi.go.id/id/publikasi/laporan/Documents/LKBI-2025.pdf, 7,916,528 bytes, downloaded and extracted in full, 464,907 characters) is the institutional report, not the financial statements. It carries only 'Tabel 1. LAPORAN POSISI KEUANGAN Per 31 Desember 2025 dan 31 Desember 2024', a summary balance sheet whose asset line 1 is 'Emas' at Rp198,350,642 million (2024: Rp106,555,642 million), with no notes at all. The report itself states that the audited document is the separate 'Laporan Keuangan Tahunan Bank Indonesia' (LKTBI), which received an unqualified (Wajar Tanpa Pengecualian) opinion from BPK RI for 2025, the 23rd consecutive year. No custody or location wording appears anywhere. Route for a later round: the LKTBI PDF itself, published at bi.go.id/id/publikasi/laporan under 'Laporan Keuangan Tahunan BI'; a 2022 edition exists at Documents/Laporan-Keuangan-Tahunan-BI-2022.pdf. Note that bi.go.id refuses curl's default HTTP/2 request with an empty reply and serves the file normally with --http1.1.

Central Bank of the UAE Annual Report 2024 (centralbank.ae/media/ymgnwy3x/2024-en-annualreport.pdf, 8,109,017 bytes, downloaded and extracted in full, 203,840 characters). The report carries a 'Financial Highlights' summary balance sheet only, with an asset line 'Gold bullion' at AED 22,982 million (2023: AED 18,147 million) and no notes to the financial statements. Every one of the seven occurrences of the word gold was read: the others are commemorative gold coin issues and commodity-market commentary. No location, institution or country is given for the bullion. Route for a later round: the CBUAE's separate audited financial statements with notes, which this annual report does not contain. The 2025 annual report URL returned by search, centralbank.ae/media/pjimtxfq/annual-report-2025-en.pdf, 404s both with and without the www host.

No PBoC financial-statement document was opened, so China has not actually been tested on this row. A single web search was not spent on it. The only PBoC document available locally was an unofficial English translation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the People's Bank of China, which is a statute and not an audited statement, and the assignment's standing instruction is not to infer. Route for a later round: whether the PBoC publishes audited annual financial statements with notes at all is the first thing to settle; its public reporting is largely the monthly balance-sheet statistics ('Balance Sheet of Monetary Authority') on pbc.gov.cn, which have no location breakdown. Treat as untested, not as a negative.

No SAMA financial-statement document was opened. Two web searches were spent and both returned almost entirely commercial-bank annual reports and Argaam/Zawya coverage of SAMA's monthly asset totals. The one SAMA-hosted annual report URL that search returned, sama.gov.sa/en-US/EconomicReports/AnnualReport/Sixtieth_Annual_Report-EN.pdf, returns HTTP 404 (717 bytes of HTML) over HTTP/1.1 and an empty reply over HTTP/2. Route for a later round: fetch SAMA's own publications index (sama.gov.sa/en-US/EconomicReports/Pages/report.aspx?cid=55 was returned by search and not opened) rather than searching by country name, per the common brief's rule. Untested, not a negative.

The State Bank of Pakistan's 'Annual Accounts of State Bank of Pakistan' PDF (sbp.org.pk/publications/anu_stats/2020/Part-2/08-Annual Accounts of State Bank of Pakistan.pdf), returned by web search, was requested three times and returned HTTP 403 with a 199-byte and then a 5,187-byte HTML body, both over HTTP/2 and over HTTP/1.1 with a generic user agent. The brief forbids spoofing a browser user agent, so the file was not obtained and the gold note was never read. Route for a later round: try WebFetch rather than curl on the same path, or the consolidated/unconsolidated financial statements under sbp.org.pk/Reports/Annual/FS/, several editions of which web search returned. Untested, not a negative.

No Bank of Papua New Guinea financial statements were opened. A locally available copy of the Auditor-General of Papua New Guinea's 'Part IV Report of the Auditor-General 2024 on the Accounts of Public Authorities and Statutory Bodies' (4,260,612 bytes, extracted in full) was grepped: its Bank of Papua New Guinea section is an audit-opinion summary and its only reference to gold is the statutory statement that the Bank is to 'manage the gold, foreign exchange and other international reserves of PNG'. That is a mechanism, not a location, and the common brief rules it out as a record. Route for a later round: BPNG's own annual report financial statements at bankpng.gov.pg.
